name: CALIPER artifact
alternateName: Corpus of ALternative LLM Inputs for Paraphrase Evaluation and Robustness
description: CALIPER is a prompt-robustness dataset and benchmark snapshot built from Alpaca, GSM8K, and MMLU prompts. It contains the canonical CALIPER prompt paraphrases, model generations, response-quality metric scores, content-preservation scores, and Croissant/Responsible AI metadata for robustness analysis.
citeAs: Anonymous. CALIPER: Corpus of ALternative LLM Inputs for Paraphrase Evaluation and Robustness. 2026.

rai:dataCollection: Base prompts were selected from existing public benchmark resources (Alpaca, GSM8K, and MMLU). Paraphrase variants were generated using style templates and then scored for semantic content preservation. Model responses and response-quality scores were generated as evaluation artifacts.
rai:dataCollectionRawData: Source prompt material comes from Alpaca, GSM8K, and MMLU. CALIPER adds generated paraphrases, generated model responses, automated content-preservation scores, automated response-quality scores, style-to-tag mappings, and the canonical mirrored CALIPER release files from source commit 3a340c6185b0fc9ebae7ea7601d421a622ce6dad.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Records are organized by dataset, prompt identifier, paraphrase style key, tag family, generated response, content-preservation score, and metric score vector.
Analyses reported in the paper condition on content-preservation scores of at least 4.
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Each paraphrase receives a 0--5 content-preservation score comparing the original prompt and paraphrase.
Each model response receives ten 0--10 task-quality scores.
All reported automated scores used gemini-2.5-flash-preview-05-20 as the judge model, run in September 2025 with deterministic decoding.
rai:dataAnnotationPlatform: Gemini 2.5 Flash Preview judge model for automated scoring
rai:annotationsPerItem: One automated content-preservation score is recorded for each prompt-style pair where scoring is available. One vector of ten automated task-quality scores is recorded for each scored model response.
rai:machineAnnotationTools: gemini-2.5-flash-preview-05-20 for content-preservation and task-quality scores; all reported automated scores used this judge model, run in September 2025 with deterministic decoding (temperature 0).
rai:dataLimitations: The benchmark measures robustness to text prompt paraphrases and should not be treated as a complete evaluation of all LLM reliability properties.
Content preservation is judged from an average English reader perspective, which may under-credit multilingual, encoded, or dialectal variants that are meaningful to other users.
The reported benchmark snapshot covers a limited set of open-weight instruction models and deterministic decoding.
Automated judge scores may reflect preferences or blind spots of the judge model and should be audited for high-stakes use.
rai:dataUseCases: Evaluating LLM robustness to meaning-preserving prompt rewording.
Auditing failure modes by paraphrase style and tag family.
Developing paraphrase-aware evaluation, training, and mitigation methods.
Inspecting average-case and worst-style robustness gaps across tasks and models.
rai:dataSocialImpact: CALIPER is intended to improve transparency about prompt sensitivity and to help identify robustness gaps affecting users with different wording styles, registers, dialects, and formatting habits. It could also be misused to search for brittle prompts or bypasses, so results should be used for defensive auditing, mitigation, and responsible reporting.
rai:dataBiases: The style taxonomy reflects the authors' chosen categories and may not cover all real-world language communities or interaction styles.
Dialect and register labels are diagnostic groupings for model behavior, not judgments of linguistic quality.
Source benchmark choices shape the task distribution and may bias conclusions toward instruction following, grade-school mathematics, and moral reasoning.
rai:personalSensitiveInformation: The dataset does not intentionally collect personal data. It derives from public benchmark prompts and generated paraphrases/responses. Users should still inspect downstream samples before deploying derived artifacts.
rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The dataset is versioned on the hosting platform. The anonymous submission artifact mirrors the canonical CALIPER dataset files from source commit 3a340c6185b0fc9ebae7ea7601d421a622ce6dad and adds license and Croissant/RAI metadata. Updates should document changes to prompt files, paraphrase styles, model outputs, scoring configuration, and Croissant/RAI metadata.
